text:
lucas_sales: Heads up 5m before client demo: NeoFin POC failed when they tried to POST ~30MB of concatenated reports to /v1/generate. They got 413 and the assistant returned truncated text. Need a quick client-facing fix.

ria_engineer: 413 from the gateway. Do we have their raw request?

lucas_sales: They attached the payload example in the ticket: they embedded PDFs as base64 strings inside JSON. Curl shows Content-Type: application/json and a huge body.

sam_support: That's the issue. Our edge proxy enforces client_max_body_size=4MB by default. If you shove base64 into JSON you blow it up 33%+.

kevin_oncall: Two quick low-effort fixes for a demo:
- Client-side gzip the text and send with Content-Encoding: gzip (edge accepts compressed bodies).
- Upload the file to a short-lived presigned URL, then call our ingestion endpoint with the S3 key. We can fetch server-side and stitch into the request.

lucas_sales: They want a one-step flow for the demo (no S3). Which is faster to patch?

sam_support: Gzip is fastest. If their client is JS we can give a tiny snippet. Also warn them NOT to base64 the PDFs into JSON; send raw text or gzipped bytes.

ria_engineer: Note on tokens/pricing: even if you compress the HTTP body, tokens are calculated after decompression so you'll still pay for tokens. For demos, trim to key sections.

lucas_sales: Can you paste a minimal Node example to gzip and POST?

sam_support: Sure:
```js
// node demo: gzip and send
const zlib = require('zlib');
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const fs = require('fs');
const buf = fs.readFileSync('combined.txt');
const gz = zlib.gzipSync(buf);
await fetch('https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate?model=rwd-4x', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': 'Bearer <token>',
    'Content-Type': 'text/plain',
    'Content-Encoding': 'gzip'
  },
  body: gz
});
```

kevin_oncall: Also watch retries: the client retried blindly and hit 429s. 413 is client error; recommend no automatic retries on 413. If they see 429 use exponential backoff and honor Retry-After.

lucas_sales: Can we temporarily loosen the body size for their IP so the demo is guaranteed to work?

kevin_oncall: We can whitelist their demo IP for 1 hour and increase client_max_body_size to 50MB for that IP only. I'll file an emergency change. pinging @deploy_bot for approval.

deploy_bot: Change request CR-2024-78 submitted -> Increase proxy body limit for IP 203.0.113.44 for 60m. Requires SOC approval. ETA 18m.

ria_engineer: If whitelist is slow, fallback is presign flow. I can send a tiny presign + ingest snippet:
1) POST /presign -> returns upload_url + key
2) Client PUTs file to upload_url
3) POST /ingest { key: 's3://...' } -> we fetch and run generate
I can paste curl steps if you want.

lucas_sales: Please paste the presign cURL too, send both to the customer.

sam_support: Presign cURL (minimal):
```bash
# 1) request presign
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/presign -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"filename":"reports.zip"}'
# 2) PUT to the returned url (client)
curl -X PUT "<upload_url>" -H "Content-Type: application/zip" --upload-file reports.zip
# 3) notify ingest
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/ingest -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"source_key":"<s3_key>","model":"rwd-4x","max_tokens":1024}'
```

kevin_oncall: After the call we'll revert the whitelist and audit logs. Also capture demo session id from the customer so we can correlate logs.

lucas_sales: Got it. Sending both snippets + guidance: gzip for fastest path, presign if they prefer a single UX. Also telling them to reduce scope to avoid huge token charges.

sam_support: Final note for eng: if customers keep needing large single-request uploads, we should consider a builtin /upload+fetch flow in API docs to make the presign pattern first-class. Filing a backlog ticket.

lucas_sales: Thanks team. I'll update after the demo. :thumbsup:
